distractors.D: Device groups scope RBAC/automation for endpoints, not incident assignment.

explanation.exam_pattern: Route/track incident work = assign owner + set status (plus tags/comments).

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Manage incidents (assign, status, tags) in Microsoft Defender XDR

questions.stem: Automated investigation produced several remediation actions that are pending approval, and the team also wants to review the history of actions already taken across Microsoft Defender XDR. Which centralized hub shows and lets them approve/undo these actions?

explanation.correct: The Action center centralizes remediation actions - pending actions awaiting approval and a history of completed actions - across Defender XDR, where analysts can approve, reject, or undo them.

distractors.A: The Content hub installs Sentinel solutions; it is not the remediation action center.
distractors.C: The investigation graph (a Sentinel feature) visualizes entities; it is not the remediation-action hub.
distractors.D: Secure Score measures posture; it does not track remediation actions.

explanation.exam_pattern: Approve/track pending and completed remediation actions = Action center.

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): The Action center in Microsoft Defender XDR

questions.stem: A SOC wants to continuously improve the quality and signal of its incident queue over time. Which TWO practices support this goal? (Choose two.)

options.text: Resolve incidents with an accurate classification and determination (true/false/benign positive)
Tune or suppress alerts that are confirmed benign and noisy
Disable the Microsoft Defender XDR data connectors
Delete incidents to keep the queue short

explanation.correct: Classifying/closing incidents accurately feeds detection tuning and metrics, and tuning/suppressing confirmed-benign noisy alerts raises signal - both improve queue quality over time.

distractors.C: Disabling connectors stops data flowing in - the opposite of a healthy queue.
distractors.D: Deleting incidents destroys context and the outcome signal; it does not improve detection quality.

explanation.exam_pattern: Improve the queue = classify on close + tune/suppress confirmed-benign noise.

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Classify incidents and tune detections in Microsoft Defender XDR

questions.stem: A security team wants each open recommendation assigned to an owner with a remediation due date, and wants overdue items to drive accountability without instantly penalizing Secure Score. Which Microsoft Defender for Cloud feature provides this?

options.text: Governance rules (assign owner, due date, grace period)

explanation.correct: Governance rules assign an owner and a remediation due date (e.g., 7/14/30/90 days) to recommendations and can apply a grace period so a recommendation doesn't affect Secure Score until it becomes overdue.

distractors.A: Alert suppression dismisses specific security alerts; it does not assign recommendation ownership or due dates.
distractors.B: JIT VM access reduces port exposure; it is a control, not a remediation governance feature.
distractors.C: Workflow automation triggers Logic Apps on alerts/recommendations; it does not set owners, due dates, or grace periods.

explanation.exam_pattern: Owner + due date + grace period on recommendations = governance rules.

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Drive remediation with governance rules in Defender for Cloud

questions.stem: An organization wants to assess the operating systems and software on its Azure VMs for vulnerabilities and exposed secrets WITHOUT installing an agent on each machine. Which Defender for Cloud capability provides this?

explanation.correct: Agentless machine scanning (available with Defender CSPM or Defender for Servers Plan 2) inspects VM disks on a schedule for vulnerabilities, installed software, and secrets without deploying an in-guest agent.

distractors.A: JIT VM access controls management-port exposure; it does not scan for vulnerabilities/secrets.
distractors.C: The legacy Log Analytics agent (MMA) is agent-based collection - the opposite of agentless - and is being retired.
distractors.D: Adaptive network hardening recommends NSG rules; it is not a vulnerability/secrets scanner.

explanation.exam_pattern: Scan VM disks for vulns/secrets with no in-guest agent = agentless machine scanning.

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Agentless machine scanning in Microsoft Defender for Cloud

questions.stem: A security architect wants an outside-in view of the organization's internet-facing assets (domains, hosts, exposed services) to find unknown or unmanaged attack surface. Which capability, included with Defender CSPM, provides this discovery?

explanation.correct: External attack surface management discovers internet-facing assets from an outside-in (attacker) perspective, surfacing unknown/unmanaged exposure; it is included with Defender CSPM.

distractors.A: The regulatory compliance dashboard maps controls to standards; it does not discover external internet-facing assets.
distractors.B: JIT reduces management-port exposure on known VMs; it does not discover unknown external assets.
distractors.D: Workload protection plans provide threat detection for resource types, not external attack-surface discovery.

explanation.exam_pattern: Outside-in discovery of internet-facing assets = external attack surface management (EASM).

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): External attack surface management in Defender for Cloud

questions.stem: Where do the security recommendations shown in Microsoft Defender for Cloud come from, by default?

options.text: They are authored manually by each subscription owner
An Azure Policy initiative (the Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark) assigned to the scope

explanation.correct: Recommendations are generated by evaluating resources against a security policy - an Azure Policy initiative, by default the Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark (MCSB) - assigned at the subscription/management-group scope. You can also add custom recommendations.

distractors.A: Recommendations are produced by policy evaluation, not hand-authored per subscription.
distractors.C: Sentinel analytics rules detect threats in logs; they do not generate Defender for Cloud posture recommendations.
distractors.D: Conditional Access governs identity sign-in, not cloud-resource posture recommendations.

explanation.exam_pattern: Defender for Cloud recommendations = Azure Policy security initiative (MCSB by default).

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Security policies and the Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark

questions.stem: Auditors require the environment to be measured against PCI DSS and NIST SP 800-53 in addition to the default benchmark. How does an analyst make Defender for Cloud track these?

options.text: Add the standards to the Regulatory compliance dashboard (assign the compliance standards)
Raise the Secure Score target to 100%

explanation.correct: You add regulatory standards (PCI DSS, NIST, ISO, etc.) to the Regulatory compliance dashboard; Defender for Cloud then continuously assesses resources against those controls alongside the default MCSB.

distractors.B: JIT is a single hardening control, not a compliance-standard assessment.
distractors.C: A workbook visualizes data; it does not add a compliance standard assessment.
distractors.D: Secure Score targets don't map resources to PCI/NIST controls.

explanation.exam_pattern: Track PCI/NIST/ISO = add the standard(s) to the Regulatory compliance dashboard.

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Add regulatory standards to the compliance dashboard

questions.stem: In Microsoft Defender for Cloud, recommendations are grouped into 'security controls' for Secure Score. How are points earned for a control?

options.text: Points are fixed and cannot change with remediation
Each individual recommendation adds points independently as it is fixed
Points are earned only when ALL recommendations in the control are remediated for a given resource
Points are based on the number of alerts generated

explanation.correct: Secure Score is calculated from security controls (groups of related recommendations); a resource earns the control's points only when all of that control's recommendations are remediated for it, encouraging complete hardening.

distractors.A: Points change as you remediate; the score rises with remediation.
distractors.B: Points accrue at the control level (all recommendations satisfied), not per single recommendation.
distractors.D: Secure Score reflects posture/recommendations, not alert volume.

explanation.exam_pattern: Secure Score = per-control (all recommendations in a control remediated for a resource).

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): How Secure Score and security controls are calculated

questions.stem: Fill in the blank (one word): When a specific recommendation does not apply to a resource (for example, an accepted risk or a mitigated-by-design case) and you want it excluded so it stops affecting Secure Score, you create an ______ in Microsoft Defender for Cloud.

explanation.correct: An exemption excludes a recommendation from a resource/scope (with a justification such as waiver or risk mitigated), so it no longer impacts Secure Score or the recommendation list.
explanation.exam_pattern: Exclude a recommendation from a resource (accepted risk / mitigated) = exemption.

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Exempt resources from recommendations in Defender for Cloud

questions.stem: A team needs just-in-time VM access, file integrity monitoring, and integrated vulnerability assessment on their servers - not only the Defender for Endpoint integration. Which plan/tier is required?

explanation.correct: Defender for Servers Plan 2 provides the full capability set - JIT VM access, file integrity monitoring, integrated vulnerability assessment, agentless scanning, and more. Plan 1 delivers only the Defender for Endpoint integration.

distractors.A: Foundational CSPM is free posture management; it is not a workload protection plan.
distractors.C: Plan 1 is limited to the Defender for Endpoint integration; it lacks JIT, FIM, and VA.
distractors.D: Defender for Resource Manager monitors ARM control-plane operations, not server guest protection.

explanation.exam_pattern: JIT + FIM + VA on servers = Defender for Servers Plan 2 (Plan 1 = MDE integration only).

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Defender for Servers plans (Plan 1 vs Plan 2)

questions.stem: A company hosts web applications on Azure App Service and wants threat detection for web-app attacks and suspicious behavior on those apps. Which plan should be enabled?

explanation.correct: Defender for App Service detects threats targeting web apps running on App Service (e.g., web-attack patterns, suspicious operations) and surfaces related alerts.

distractors.B: Defender for Key Vault detects abnormal secret/key access, not web-app attacks.
distractors.C: Defender for Storage protects storage accounts (blob malware scanning, access anomalies), not App Service web apps.
distractors.D: Defender for DNS monitored DNS-layer threats and has since been consolidated; it is not the App Service plan.

explanation.exam_pattern: Threat detection for Azure App Service web apps = Defender for App Service.

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Microsoft Defender for App Service

questions.stem: A SOC wants alerts on suspicious control-plane operations - such as anomalous use of Azure Resource Manager to deploy or modify resources, or toolkit activity (e.g., from compromised credentials). Which plan detects these ARM-layer threats?

explanation.correct: Defender for Resource Manager monitors the Azure Resource Manager control plane and alerts on suspicious/malicious management operations (e.g., unusual resource deployment, exploitation toolkits).

distractors.A: Defender for Servers protects VM guests via Defender for Endpoint, not ARM operations.
distractors.B: Defender for Databases detects database-layer threats (e.g., SQL injection), not control-plane operations.
distractors.D: Defender for Containers protects Kubernetes workloads, not the ARM control plane.

explanation.exam_pattern: Suspicious ARM control-plane / management operations = Defender for Resource Manager.

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Microsoft Defender for Resource Manager

questions.stem: On protected servers, a team wants to be alerted when critical operating-system files, registry keys, or application binaries are changed, to catch tampering. Which Defender for Cloud capability provides this?

explanation.correct: File integrity monitoring (part of Defender for Servers Plan 2) tracks changes to important OS files, registry keys, and application files, alerting on potentially suspicious modifications.

distractors.A: Regulatory compliance maps controls to standards; it does not alert on file changes.
distractors.B: JIT controls management-port exposure; it does not watch file/registry changes.
distractors.D: Adaptive application controls allowlist known-good apps; they are not file-change monitoring.

explanation.exam_pattern: Alert on changes to OS/registry/app files = file integrity monitoring (FIM).

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): File integrity monitoring in Microsoft Defender for Cloud

questions.stem: An organization publishes REST APIs through Azure API Management and wants threat detection and security insights specifically for those APIs (e.g., anomalous or malicious API access). Which plan should be enabled?

explanation.correct: Defender for APIs provides threat detection and security posture insights for APIs published in Azure API Management, surfacing anomalous or malicious API usage.

distractors.A: Foundational CSPM provides posture recommendations, not API runtime threat detection.
distractors.C: Defender for App Service protects web apps hosted on App Service, not APIs managed by API Management.
distractors.D: Defender for Storage covers storage accounts, not API traffic.

explanation.exam_pattern: Threat detection for APIs in Azure API Management = Defender for APIs.

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Microsoft Defender for APIs

questions.stem: Which statement best describes how Microsoft Defender for Cloud workload protection plans are enabled?

options.text: All plans are always on and cannot be turned off
They are enabled granularly - you turn on individual Defender plans per subscription (and some per resource) as needed
Enabling any one plan automatically enables all other plans
Plans can only be enabled for the entire Azure tenant at once

explanation.correct: Defender plans are toggled individually (per subscription, and for some workloads per resource), so you can protect exactly the resource types you need and manage cost.

distractors.A: Plans are optional and can be enabled or disabled; they are not always on.
distractors.C: Enabling one plan does not enable the others; each is separate.
distractors.D: Plans are enabled at the subscription (or resource) level, not only tenant-wide.

explanation.exam_pattern: Defender plans = enabled per subscription/resource, individually (cost/scope control).

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Enable Microsoft Defender for Cloud plans

questions.stem: To receive threat alerts for the following two resource types, an organization must enable the corresponding Defender plan for EACH. Which TWO pairings are correct? (Choose two.)

options.text: Any resource -> the Regulatory compliance dashboard
Azure SQL databases -> Defender for Databases (Defender for SQL)
Azure Storage accounts -> Defender for Storage

explanation.correct: Runtime threat alerts for SQL databases require Defender for Databases/SQL, and for storage accounts require Defender for Storage - each resource type has its own workload plan.

distractors.A: The Regulatory compliance dashboard maps controls to standards; it is not a threat-alert plan.
distractors.D: Secure Score is free posture management; it does not provide resource threat alerts.

explanation.exam_pattern: Threat alerts are per-plan: SQL -> Defender for Databases; Storage -> Defender for Storage.

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Workload protection plans by resource type

questions.stem: With Defender for Servers Plan 2 enabled, where do the discovered CVEs/weaknesses on a protected virtual machine appear for the analyst to review and prioritize?

options.text: As vulnerability assessment findings/recommendations (via the integrated Defender Vulnerability Management scanner)

explanation.correct: Defender for Servers integrates Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management, so VM software vulnerabilities (CVEs) surface as assessment findings and security recommendations to triage and remediate.

distractors.B: Watchlists are Sentinel reference data, not VM vulnerability findings.
distractors.C: Quarantine policies are a Defender for Office 365 construct, unrelated to VM vulnerabilities.
distractors.D: Conditional Access reports cover sign-in policy, not VM CVEs.

explanation.exam_pattern: Server CVEs with Defender for Servers = integrated vulnerability assessment (MDVM) findings/recommendations.

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Vulnerability assessment for machines in Defender for Cloud

questions.stem: A team wants Microsoft Defender for Cloud to continuously send its alerts and recommendations to a Log Analytics workspace and to an Event Hub (to feed a third-party SIEM). Which feature is designed for this?

explanation.correct: Continuous export streams Defender for Cloud alerts and recommendations to a Log Analytics workspace or Event Hub, enabling downstream integration (e.g., a third-party SIEM).

distractors.A: Secure Score measures posture; it is not an export pipeline.
distractors.B: JIT controls management-port exposure; it does not export alerts.
distractors.C: Alert suppression quiets specific alerts; it does not export data.

explanation.exam_pattern: Stream Defender for Cloud alerts/recommendations out (Log Analytics / Event Hub) = continuous export.

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Continuously export Microsoft Defender for Cloud data

questions.stem: Before an incident occurs, a SOC wants to validate that their Defender for Cloud alert pipeline and automation (exports, playbooks) actually fire. What is the safe, supported way to produce test alerts?

options.text: Run real malware on a production VM
Generate sample alerts from Microsoft Defender for Cloud

explanation.correct: Defender for Cloud can generate sample alerts, letting teams validate alert routing, exports, and automation end to end without a real attack.

distractors.A: Running real malware is dangerous and unnecessary; sample alerts exist for safe testing.
distractors.B: Secure Score targets are unrelated to generating test alerts.
distractors.C: Deleting resources is destructive and does not validate the alert pipeline.

explanation.exam_pattern: Safely test the alert/automation pipeline = generate sample alerts.

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Generate sample security alerts in Defender for Cloud

questions.stem: Microsoft Defender for Cloud observes several related alerts on the same resources that appear to be stages of one attack. How does Defender for Cloud help the analyst see the bigger picture?

options.text: It deletes the lower-severity alerts automatically
It correlates related alerts into a security incident
It converts the alerts into recommendations

explanation.correct: Defender for Cloud correlates related alerts into a single security incident, grouping the stages of an attack so analysts can respond to the whole story rather than isolated alerts.

distractors.A: Correlating alerts does not change Secure Score (which reflects recommendations).
distractors.B: Related alerts are grouped, not deleted; evidence is preserved.
distractors.D: Alerts are detected threats; they are not converted into posture recommendations.

explanation.exam_pattern: Related Defender for Cloud alerts grouped into one attack view = a security incident.

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Security alerts and incidents in Microsoft Defender for Cloud

questions.stem: An organization wants the right people emailed automatically whenever a high-severity Microsoft Defender for Cloud alert fires on a subscription. Which setting enables this?

options.text: Email notifications (configured per subscription by severity/role)

explanation.correct: Defender for Cloud email notification settings let you choose who is emailed (by role such as Owner, and by minimum alert severity) when alerts occur on a subscription.

distractors.B: Quarantine policies are a Defender for Office 365 construct, unrelated to alert emails.
distractors.C: Watchlists are Sentinel reference data; they do not send Defender for Cloud alert emails.
distractors.D: JIT reduces port exposure; it does not notify on alerts.

explanation.exam_pattern: Email the right people on high-severity alerts = Defender for Cloud email notifications (by severity/role).

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Configure email notifications for security alerts

questions.stem: After investigation, an analyst concludes a Defender for Cloud alert is a false positive. They set the alert status to 'Dismissed'. What does dismissing the alert signify?

options.text: The alert is permanently prevented from ever recurring
The Defender plan is turned off
The alert is closed as not requiring action (e.g., false positive), without remediating a threat

explanation.correct: Dismissing marks the alert as not actionable (such as a false positive or benign), closing it in the queue; it records the outcome but does not, by itself, stop similar future alerts.

distractors.A: To stop a recurring benign pattern you use a suppression rule; dismissing a single alert does not prevent recurrence.
distractors.B: Dismissing changes the alert status; it does not delete resources.
distractors.C: Dismissing one alert does not disable the plan.

explanation.exam_pattern: Dismiss = close as not actionable; suppress = stop a recurring benign pattern.

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Manage and respond to security alerts (alert status)

questions.stem: An organization wants to manage Microsoft Sentinel together with Defender XDR in the unified Microsoft Defender portal. What is a key prerequisite/consideration for onboarding?

options.text: Every user needs the Global Administrator role
You onboard a Log Analytics workspace that has Microsoft Sentinel enabled (one primary workspace to the unified portal)
Sentinel must be moved to an Azure Storage account
You must delete the Log Analytics workspace first

explanation.correct: Sentinel runs on a Log Analytics workspace with Sentinel enabled; onboarding to the Defender portal connects that workspace (one primary workspace) so XDR and Sentinel share one incident queue.

distractors.A: Global Administrator is not required for every user; least-privilege roles are used.
distractors.C: Sentinel data stays in Log Analytics; it is not moved to a storage account.
distractors.D: Deleting the workspace would destroy all Sentinel data; the workspace is required.

explanation.exam_pattern: Unified portal = onboard the Sentinel-enabled Log Analytics workspace (one primary workspace).

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Connect Microsoft Sentinel to the Microsoft Defender portal

questions.stem: An engineer needs to create and edit Microsoft Sentinel analytics rules and manage content, but should not be granted broad subscription Owner rights. Which built-in role is the least-privilege fit?

explanation.correct: Microsoft Sentinel Contributor allows creating and editing analytics rules, workbooks, and other content (on top of read and incident management) - the least-privilege role for authoring detections.

distractors.A: Responder adds incident management but not rule authoring.
distractors.B: Subscription Owner is far broader than needed for authoring Sentinel content.
distractors.C: Reader can only view; it cannot create or edit rules.

explanation.exam_pattern: Author/edit analytics rules = Sentinel Contributor; triage only = Responder; view = Reader.

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Roles and permissions in Microsoft Sentinel

questions.stem: A company keeps two Microsoft Sentinel workspaces (one per region) and needs a single KQL query that returns results from a table in BOTH workspaces. Which approach works?

options.text: It is impossible to query more than one workspace
Export both to a CSV and merge manually
Move all data into a single Azure SQL database
Use the workspace() expression to reference the other workspace and union the results (cross-workspace query)

explanation.correct: Cross-workspace queries use the workspace("...") expression (often with union) so a single KQL query spans tables across multiple workspaces - useful for multi-region or multi-tenant SOCs.

distractors.A: Multi-workspace querying is supported via the workspace() expression.
distractors.B: Manual CSV merging is not a query mechanism and does not scale.
distractors.C: Sentinel data lives in Log Analytics; moving it to SQL is neither required nor how cross-workspace queries work.

explanation.exam_pattern: Query across workspaces = workspace("name").Table (+ union) cross-workspace query.

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Query multiple workspaces in Microsoft Sentinel

questions.stem: A managed security service provider (MSSP) needs its analysts to manage many customers' Microsoft Sentinel workspaces from its own tenant, with delegated, auditable access. Which Azure capability is designed for this cross-tenant management?

explanation.correct: Azure Lighthouse enables delegated, cross-tenant resource management, so an MSSP can manage multiple customers' Sentinel workspaces from a single pane with scoped, auditable access.

distractors.B: Conditional Access App Control is a Defender for Cloud Apps session-control feature, not MSSP delegation.
distractors.C: Entra Connect syncs on-prem identities to Entra ID; it is not cross-tenant Azure resource delegation.
distractors.D: Watchlists are reference data in a workspace; they do not provide cross-tenant management.

explanation.exam_pattern: MSSP managing many tenants' Sentinel workspaces = Azure Lighthouse (delegated management).

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Manage multiple tenants with Azure Lighthouse and Microsoft Sentinel

questions.stem: A SOC ingests high-value security logs that must be available for real-time scheduled analytics rules and frequent interactive hunting. Which Log Analytics table plan should these tables use?

explanation.correct: The Analytics table plan is for high-value data used in continuous monitoring, real-time detection, and frequent analytics - and it is the plan scheduled analytics rules require.

distractors.A: Basic logs are for medium-touch, occasional troubleshooting data with limited query features; scheduled analytics rules can't run on Basic tables.
distractors.B: Archive is long-term retention, not an interactive query plan for real-time detection.
distractors.D: Auxiliary (data lake) logs are low-cost, low-touch data for verbose logs/compliance, not real-time detection.

explanation.exam_pattern: Real-time detection + frequent hunting = Analytics tier; cheap/low-touch = Basic/Auxiliary.

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Manage data tiers (Analytics, Basic, Auxiliary) in Microsoft Sentinel

questions.stem: Compliance requires keeping certain security logs for seven years, but analysts only query the last 90 days interactively. What is the cost-appropriate way to meet this in Log Analytics/Microsoft Sentinel?

options.text: Delete data after 90 days and hope it isn't needed
Set interactive retention short and configure long-term (archive) retention for the rest (up to 12 years total)
Keep all data in interactive retention for seven years

explanation.correct: Configure a shorter interactive retention and extend long-term (archive) retention for the remainder - total retention can reach up to 12 years - meeting compliance cost-effectively.

distractors.A: Deleting data needed for compliance fails the requirement.
distractors.C: Email is not a retention mechanism and cannot hold log volumes.
distractors.D: Keeping everything hot for seven years is far more expensive than using archive retention.

explanation.exam_pattern: Short interactive + long-term archive retention (up to 12 years) for compliance.

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Configure interactive and long-term data retention

questions.stem: Within one Log Analytics workspace, a team should be able to read only ONE specific table (for example, a sensitive application log), not all tables. Which approach grants this?

options.text: Table-level RBAC (Azure role scoped to the specific table)
Making everyone a Sentinel Reader on the workspace

explanation.correct: Table-level RBAC grants access to specific tables within a workspace, so a group can read only the designated table rather than all workspace data.

distractors.B: Watchlists store reference data; they are not an access-control mechanism.
distractors.C: Workbooks visualize data the viewer can already access; they do not grant per-table permissions.
distractors.D: Sentinel Reader on the workspace grants read across its data - broader than one table.

explanation.exam_pattern: Restrict access to a single table within a workspace = table-level RBAC.

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Manage access to Microsoft Sentinel data by table (table-level RBAC)

questions.stem: Fill in the blank (one word, plural): To satisfy EU data-residency rules while running a single SOC, an organization can deploy multiple Microsoft Sentinel ______, each created in the region where its data must stay.

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Design Microsoft Sentinel workspace architecture for residency

questions.stem: To ingest Windows Security event logs from servers into Microsoft Sentinel and control exactly which events are collected (All, Common, or Minimal), which collection method is used?

options.text: The Windows Security Events connector via the Azure Monitor Agent, configured by a data collection rule (DCR)

questions.stem: An appliance sends plain Syslog messages (not CEF) to a Linux forwarder running the Azure Monitor Agent. Into which Microsoft Sentinel table does this data land?

distractors.C: SecurityAlert holds alerts from connected products, not raw Syslog.

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Syslog and CEF data in Microsoft Sentinel (Syslog vs CommonSecurityLog)

questions.stem: A team needs a data connector for a SaaS product that exposes a REST API, but they want to avoid writing and hosting custom code. Which Microsoft Sentinel capability lets them build the connector declaratively?

distractors.D: A watchlist imports reference data, not a streaming API connector.

explanation.exam_pattern: Build a REST-API connector without code = Codeless Connector Platform (CCP).

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Create a codeless connector for Microsoft Sentinel

questions.stem: A custom in-house application writes JSON logs that a team wants to send into a custom table in their Log Analytics workspace for Microsoft Sentinel. Which mechanism is intended for sending such custom data?

options.text: The Logs ingestion API (with a data collection rule to a custom table)

distractors.C: A session policy is a Defender for Cloud Apps control, unrelated to log ingestion.
distractors.D: TAXII ingests STIX threat indicators, not arbitrary custom app logs.

explanation.exam_pattern: Send custom app logs to a custom table = Logs ingestion API + DCR.

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Send custom logs with the Logs ingestion API

questions.stem: An organization wants to bring Amazon Web Services logs (for example CloudTrail) into Microsoft Sentinel. Which ingestion method does the AWS connector commonly use?

options.text: Pulling logs from an AWS S3 bucket (S3-based connector)
Installing the Azure Monitor Agent on every EC2 instance

questions.stem: A SOC wants to verify that its data connectors are healthy and ingesting, and be alerted if a connector stops sending data. Which capability surfaces connector health/status in Microsoft Sentinel?

options.text: Health monitoring (the SentinelHealth table / connector health)

distractors.D: The investigation graph visualizes an incident's entities; it does not report connector health.

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Monitor the health of your data connectors in Microsoft Sentinel

questions.stem: After installing a solution from the Content hub, a new analyst notices no data is flowing and no detections are firing. What is typically still required?

options.text: Nothing - installing a solution automatically ingests data and enables all rules
Connect/configure the solution's data connector and enable its analytics rule templates

questions.stem: When configuring Syslog/CEF or Windows event collection today, which agent should be used, given the retirement of the legacy agent?

options.text: The Azure Monitor Agent (AMA), with collection defined by data collection rules

explanation.correct: The Azure Monitor Agent (AMA) is the current agent; collection is controlled by data collection rules. The legacy Log Analytics agent (MMA/OMS) has been retired and should not be used for new deployments.

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Migrate to the Azure Monitor Agent for Microsoft Sentinel

questions.stem: Fill in the blank (one table name): Firewall logs forwarded in Common Event Format (CEF) and collected by the Azure Monitor Agent are stored in Microsoft Sentinel's ______ table.

questions.stem: In a scheduled analytics rule, what is the purpose of entity mapping?

questions.stem: When configuring a scheduled analytics rule, how do the 'run query every' and 'lookup data from the last' settings differ?

questions.stem: An automation rule fails to run a playbook, with a permissions error. What is the usual cause/fix?

The analytics rule must be deleted

questions.stem: A team wants Microsoft Defender XDR incidents and the underlying advanced-hunting events available in Microsoft Sentinel. Which data connector should they enable?

questions.stem: Which Microsoft Sentinel analytics rule type runs a KQL query on a schedule over a defined lookback period and is the most common, customizable detection type?

distractors.C: Lateral movement covers techniques such as pass-the-hash / overpass-the-hash to move between hosts.
distractors.D: MDI's phases are reconnaissance, compromised credentials, lateral movement, and domain dominance; exfiltration is not one of its named phases.

explanation.exam_pattern: MDI phases: reconnaissance -> compromised credentials -> lateral movement -> domain dominance (DCSync, Golden Ticket).

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Investigate Microsoft Defender for Identity security alerts

questions.stem: A SOC wants Defender for Identity to alert whenever a normally dormant decoy account is used, because any activity on it is suspicious. Which configuration supports this?

options.text: Tag the account as a sensitive account
Add the account to a device group
Tag the account as a honeytoken account

explanation.correct: Honeytoken entity tags mark decoy accounts that should never be used; MDI treats any authentication or activity involving them as suspicious and alerts on it.

distractors.A: Excluding the account would suppress alerts - the opposite of the goal.
distractors.B: The sensitive tag flags high-value accounts to prioritize them, but does not make any use of the account inherently suspicious like a decoy.
distractors.C: Device groups organize endpoints in Defender for Endpoint, not AD decoy accounts in MDI.

explanation.exam_pattern: Decoy/trap account = honeytoken tag; high-value account prioritization = sensitive tag.

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Configure entity tags (sensitive and honeytoken) in Defender for Identity

questions.stem: Fill in the blank (three words): Defender for Identity can visualize a ______ ______ ______ (abbreviated LMP) - a graph showing how an attacker could pivot from an exposed, non-sensitive account to a sensitive account using shared local-admin credentials.

explanation.correct: Lateral movement paths (LMPs) graphically show how an attacker could move from an exposed, non-sensitive account to a sensitive account via shared credentials.
explanation.exam_pattern: MDI's graph of pivot routes to sensitive accounts = lateral movement paths (LMPs).

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Understand lateral movement paths in Defender for Identity

questions.stem: Leadership asks which unsanctioned cloud apps ('shadow IT') employees use, based on network traffic. Which Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps capability provides this?

options.text: Conditional Access App Control session policies

explanation.correct: Cloud Discovery analyzes traffic logs (e.g., from Defender for Endpoint or firewalls) to reveal which cloud apps are used and their risk, exposing shadow IT.

distractors.A: File policies scan content in connected apps; they do not reveal which apps are in use from traffic.
distractors.B: Session policies control actions within an already-sanctioned app's session; they do not discover unknown apps.
distractors.D: App governance monitors OAuth-connected apps' permissions and behavior, not network-based discovery.

explanation.exam_pattern: Find shadow IT from traffic = Cloud Discovery; control a live session = session policy.

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Discover and manage shadow IT with Defender for Cloud Apps

questions.stem: A company allows SharePoint Online access from unmanaged devices but must block file downloads during those sessions in real time. Which Defender for Cloud Apps control does this?

options.text: A session policy (via Conditional Access App Control)

explanation.correct: Session policies, delivered through Conditional Access App Control (a reverse proxy that Entra Conditional Access routes sessions to), enforce real-time controls such as blocking downloads on unmanaged devices.

distractors.A: Cloud Discovery surfaces app usage; it cannot block an action inside a live session.
distractors.C: Activity policies alert or act on logged activities after the fact via API, not inline during the session.
distractors.D: OAuth app policies govern third-party app consent and permissions, not in-session downloads.

explanation.exam_pattern: Real-time in-session control (block download/copy) = session policy + Conditional Access App Control.

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Create session policies with Conditional Access App Control

questions.stem: After discovering a risky app, the SOC tags it 'Unsanctioned' and wants that block automatically enforced on managed endpoints. Which integration enforces the block on devices?

options.text: Defender for Cloud Apps integration with Defender for Endpoint

explanation.correct: When Defender for Cloud Apps is integrated with Defender for Endpoint, tagging an app Unsanctioned pushes the block to onboarded devices (via network protection), enforcing it even off the corporate network.

distractors.A: Conditional Access governs sign-in to apps, not blocking an unsanctioned domain on the endpoint itself.
distractors.B: Sentinel playbooks automate SOAR responses but are not the mechanism that pushes app blocks to endpoints.
distractors.C: Purview handles data governance and compliance, not endpoint network blocking of apps.

explanation.exam_pattern: Unsanctioned-app enforcement on endpoints = Defender for Cloud Apps + Defender for Endpoint integration.

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Govern discovered apps using Defender for Endpoint

questions.stem: The SOC wants out-of-the-box detection of 'impossible travel' and activity from infrequent countries for connected cloud apps, with minimal setup. Which policy type provides this?

explanation.correct: Anomaly detection policies use built-in behavioral/ML baselines to flag behaviors such as impossible travel and activity from an infrequent country - enabled by default with little configuration.

distractors.B: Access policies allow or block sign-ins in real time; they do not model behavioral baselines.
distractors.C: File policies inspect content (e.g., sensitive data in files), not behavioral anomalies like impossible travel.
distractors.D: Cloud Discovery policies watch for new or risky discovered apps, not user-behavior anomalies in connected apps.

explanation.exam_pattern: Impossible travel / behavioral anomalies out of the box = anomaly detection policies.

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Anomaly detection policies in Defender for Cloud Apps

questions.stem: In the Microsoft Defender portal, related alerts from endpoints, email, identities, and cloud apps that belong to the same attack are automatically grouped into a single what?

explanation.correct: Defender XDR correlates related alerts across endpoints, email, identities, and cloud apps that share entities into a single incident representing the full attack story.

distractors.B: Secure Score recommendations improve posture; they are unrelated to alert correlation.
distractors.C: Custom detection rules generate alerts from queries; they do not aggregate alerts across products.
distractors.D: Advanced hunting queries proactively search raw data; they are not the automatic grouping of alerts.

explanation.exam_pattern: Auto-grouped cross-workload alerts = one XDR incident (the attack story).

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Incidents and alerts in the Microsoft Defender portal

questions.stem: An analyst triages a multistage incident in the Defender portal. Which TWO are appropriate FIRST steps to understand its full scope? (Choose two.)

options.text: Delete the incident to clear the queue
Immediately reset the passwords of every user in the tenant
Review the incident's attack story / alert timeline across all assets
Open the impacted user and device entity pages for context

explanation.correct: Start by reading the incident's correlated attack story / timeline and pivoting into the affected user and device entity pages to understand scope before taking action.

distractors.A: Deleting or clearing an active incident destroys context and does not investigate scope.
distractors.B: Resetting every user is disproportionate and is not a triage step; scope the affected entities first.

explanation.exam_pattern: Triage first = understand scope via the attack story + entity pages, then targeted response.

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Investigate incidents in Microsoft Defender XDR

questions.stem: After confirming an incident is a real breach and remediating it, how should the analyst close it in the Defender portal so detection quality is tracked correctly?

options.text: Resolve it and set the classification to True positive with the appropriate determination
Create a Secure Score exception for it

explanation.correct: Resolving the incident and classifying it (True positive, with a determination) feeds back into tuning and reporting on detection accuracy.

distractors.B: Deleting alerts removes evidence and still does not record a classification.
distractors.C: Leaving it open skews the queue and loses the outcome signal.
distractors.D: Secure Score exceptions relate to posture recommendations, not incident closure.

explanation.exam_pattern: Close incidents with a classification (true/false/benign positive) to improve tuning and metrics.

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Manage and classify incidents in Microsoft Defender XDR

questions.stem: An organization has onboarded Microsoft Sentinel to Microsoft Defender XDR in the unified portal. Where do analysts now manage a single, correlated incident queue spanning both?

options.text: In the Microsoft Defender portal (security.microsoft.com), which now hosts Sentinel
Only in the Microsoft Purview portal
In the Microsoft Entra admin center
Only in the Azure portal's Microsoft Sentinel blade

explanation.correct: The Microsoft Defender portal now hosts Microsoft Sentinel, giving a single unified incident queue that correlates Defender XDR and Sentinel data.

distractors.B: Purview is for compliance and data governance, not the SOC incident queue.
distractors.C: The Entra admin center manages identities, not the unified incident queue.
distractors.D: With the unified experience, incidents are managed in the Defender portal, not restricted to the Azure Sentinel blade.

explanation.exam_pattern: Unified SOC = Sentinel onboarded into the Defender portal; one incident queue.

references: Microsoft Learn (SC-200): Microsoft Sentinel in the Microsoft Defender portal
